doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The drum battle with Ginger Baker at the Lyceum
summary: A Melody Maker spat led to a London concert with Ginger Baker's Air Force, then a tour.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So that’s 1970, and now that Keiko has mentioned Ginger Baker, I was living in Europe and I remember reading Melody Maker and seeing “Drum Battle: Ginger Baker v. Elvin Jones” Talk about that! That was quite something.

That happened from one of Albert’s articles in Life or maybe in Melody Maker. He wrote this article and he had asked me over to his apartment and he was making all these recordings and he was saying, “What do you think of this guy, what do you think of that guy?” And so I just said, “Well he’s a good drummer” and that was Mitch Mitchell. And then he played Ginger Baker playing a solo and I said, “Well I don’t know who that is but you should make him an astronaut and loose his ass!” (Laughs)
I remember reading that article! (Laughs)

Then we had this thing going in the Melody Maker. So he set up a concert in the Lyceum Theatre in London and that’s where that drum battle or whatever it was. It wasn’t a battle for me! I just sat there and it was pretty noisy.
Was it unaccompanied drumming? Did you have any accompanied musicians?
Well it was Ginger’s band.
Oh it was his band?
Air Force.
Oh Ginger Baker’s Air Force. I saw that band.
It was a good band but it was loud.
So he set up both of you with the band?

Ginger was in front of me with his drum set and I was sort of in back of him to his right. And the band was right of the middle of it. In the first place, I didn’t know what they were playing (Laughs) I had no idea.
Was there a rehearsal?
No this was the concert!
Oh you went straight to the concert?
It was something!
So he would solo and then?

We’d trade and go back and forth like that. Then we went to another place, and where was that? Yeah he went on a tour after that and we went along with him. It was a lot of fun and it sort of resolved the argument in the Melody Maker. They built that up pretty good. There wasn’t and empty seat in that place, it was packed.

I remember waiting to see what the results were. I could probably find the article if I went digging it up. But I remember the accounts. The reporter said. “Well it looked like it was an even battle pretty much but when Elvin would play the audience didn’t really understand what he was doing, and when Ginger would play, they knew him so they’d all

clap.” But I guess the reviewer favored what you were doing because maybe he was a little more intelligent than some of the audience members. He said that what you were doing was way beyond the comprehension of the audience and therefore if one had to judge it on the applause then Ginger would have won cause they favored him. But this reporter understood that what you were doing was well beyond what they could even begin to comprehend. So I don’t know if you had a feeling from the audience about your participation in that?
Well, I tell you it was hard to hear anything. I tell you, it’s loud. I don’t see how they could do it. I said, “Oh God, I couldn’t do that everyday.” I’d have to wear earplugs or something.
